## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Mahāniddesa-aṭṭhakathā*, also known by the title *Saddhammapajjotikā*, is the commentary on the *Mahāniddesa* in the Khuddakanikāya section of the Pali commentarial corpus (*Aṭṭhakathā*) [Norman 1983]. It is known in modern scholarship through publications such as the Hewavitarne (Simon Hewavitarne Bequest) edition [Adikaram 1946], and is routinely cited in historical and doctrinal surveys of Pali Buddhism [Adikaram 1946; Karunadasa 1967].
According to DharmaNexus match data, the text demonstrates extensive Pali-internal textual reuse, sharing 57,527 passages across 498 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its most prominent alignments are with other major Theravāda commentaries and treatises, foremost the *Paṭisambhidāmagga-aṭṭhakathā* (over 378,000 matched characters, with a continuous alignment between segments §629_4–696_5 and §850_6–907_15), the *Majjhimanikāye Mūlapaṇṇāsa-aṭṭhakathā* (§642_1–672_1 aligning with §299_8–318_11), the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Vibhaṅga-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathā*, both parts of the *Visuddhimagga*, the *Pārājikakaṇḍa-aṭṭhakathā*, and its companion volume the *Cūḷaniddesa-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus records no cross-language matches with score 10 or greater [DharmaNexus].
